title: Cacio e Pepe-Style Spaghetti with Pecorino and Butter
description: Spaghetti tossed with grated pecorino, plenty of black pepper and starchy pasta water until glossy. A spoon of butter keeps the sauce from clumping. About $1.75 a plate.
notes: Grate the pecorino as finely as you can; coarse shreds melt slowly and turn stringy. The most common problem is clumping, which happens when the pan is too hot, so take the skillet off the heat before the cheese goes in. Cook the pasta in less water than usual so the water is cloudy with starch; that starch is what makes the sauce. Parmesan cheese can replace up to half the pecorino for a milder, less salty sauce, with the same allergens. Traditional pecorino is made with animal rennet, so strict vegetarians should look for a vegetarian-rennet cheese. This is best eaten right away; leftovers keep in the refrigerator up to 3 days (refrigerate within 2 hours) and reheat best in a skillet with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: finely grated pecorino romano (about 120 g), plus more for serving
freshly ground black pepper, coarsely ground
kosher salt, for the pasta water
water, for cooking the pasta (about 3 quarts)

instructions: Bring about 3 quarts of water to a boil in a large pot and add the kosher salt. Using less water than usual concentrates the starch you will need for the sauce.
While the water heats, toast the black pepper in a dry 12-inch skillet over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the butter, let it melt, then take the skillet off the heat.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes less than the package says. It should still be firm in the center.

Ladle 1 1/2 cups of the cloudy pasta water into a measuring cup, then move the spaghetti straight into the skillet with tongs. Add 1/2 cup of the pasta water and toss over medium-low heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until the pasta is just tender and the water has thickened slightly.
Take the skillet off the heat and let it sit for 30 seconds. In a small bowl, stir the pecorino with 1/4 cup of the warm pasta water into a loose paste.

Add the cheese paste to the spaghetti and toss quickly and constantly with tongs, adding more pasta water a splash at a time, until the sauce is smooth, creamy and clings to each strand. Serve immediately with extra pecorino and pepper.

title: Egg Fried Rice with Peas, Carrots and Scallions
description: Day-old jasmine rice stir-fried hot with softly scrambled eggs, frozen peas and carrots, and scallions, seasoned with soy sauce. A good use for leftover rice at about $1.25 a plate.
notes: Cold, cooked rice is the key: freshly cooked rice is too moist and turns mushy, so cook it a day ahead or spread hot rice on a tray and chill it uncovered for an hour. Break up clumps with your hands before cooking so every grain gets coated. For gluten-free fried rice, use gluten-free tamari in place of the soy sauce, which removes wheat but keeps soy. Leftover cooked chicken or ham can go in with the peas, which makes it no longer vegetarian. Cooked rice should be refrigerated within 2 hours, because rice left out can grow bacteria that reheating does not destroy. Keeps covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days; reheat in a skillet or microwave until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: cold cooked jasmine rice (about 600 g), clumps broken up
frozen peas and diced carrots (140 g), no need to thaw
scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens kept separate

instructions: Crack the eggs into a small bowl, add the salt and beat until no streaks of white remain.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs and stir gently for 45 to 60 seconds, just until they form soft, slightly wet curds. Slide them onto a plate.

Return the pan to high heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil. Add the scallion whites and stir for 20 seconds, then add the frozen peas and carrots and cook for 2 minutes, until hot and bright.

Add the rice and press it flat against the pan. Let it sit undisturbed for 1 minute to toast, then toss and spread it out again. Repeat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the rice is hot and some grains are lightly crisp.
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edge of the pan so it sizzles, then toss to coat. Return the eggs, breaking them into bite-size pieces, and add the scallion greens and a few grinds of pepper.
Toss for 1 more minute, taste, and add a pinch more salt or a little more soy sauce if needed. Serve hot.

title: Lemon Garlic Butter Shrimp with Rice
description: Large shrimp seared fast and finished in a garlicky lemon butter pan sauce, spooned over fluffy long-grain rice. Frozen shrimp keeps it to about $3 a plate, and dinner is ready in 30 minutes.
notes: Shrimp is done when it is opaque and pink all the way through and curled into a loose C shape, about 120°F in the thickest part for tender shrimp; the USDA guideline for seafood is 145°F, so cook a minute longer if you prefer that. Tightly curled O-shaped shrimp are overcooked and rubbery. Frozen shrimp is usually the cheapest choice: thaw it overnight in the refrigerator or in a bowl of cold water for 15 minutes, then pat it very dry so it sears instead of steaming. Olive oil can replace the butter for a dairy-free version, which removes the milk allergen. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 2 days; reheat gently in a covered skillet with a splash of water just until hot (165°F), since shrimp toughens quickly.

ingredients.name: long grain white rice (280 g), rinsed
large shrimp, peeled and deveined, thawed if frozen (680 g)
lemon, zested and juiced (about 3 tbsp juice)

instructions: Combine the rinsed rice, water and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes, then take the pan off the heat and let it stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
While the rice cooks, pat the shrimp very dry with paper towels and toss with the remaining 3/4 teaspoon of salt and the pepper.

Heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook without moving for 1 1/2 minutes, until pink and lightly browned underneath.
Turn the shrimp and cook for 1 minute more, until nearly opaque. Move them to a plate; they will finish cooking in the sauce.
Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter and the garlic. Cook, stirring, for 45 to 60 seconds, until the garlic is fragrant and pale gold but not brown.

Stir in the lemon juice and zest, then return the shrimp and any juices on the plate. Toss for 30 to 60 seconds, until the shrimp are opaque and pink all the way through and coated in glossy sauce. Taste for salt.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the shrimp and every bit of the lemon garlic butter from the pan.

title: Honey-Mustard Chicken Thighs with Roasted Carrots
description: Bone-in thighs roasted over carrots and brushed with a honey, Dijon and garlic glaze that drips into the pan. Crisp skin, sticky-sweet carrots, one pan, about $2.50 a plate.
notes: Pat the chicken very dry so the skin crisps before the glaze goes on; glazing too early makes the honey burn. Chicken must reach at least 165°F in the thickest part, and thighs are more tender at 175°F to 185°F. Pure maple syrup can replace the honey, and parsnips or wedges of sweet potato can stand in for some of the carrots. Most Dijon mustard is gluten-free, but check the label if that matters. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat at 375°F for about 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F. Cooled cooked chicken freezes for up to 3 months.

ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 2 1/2 lb, 1.1 kg)
carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch sticks (680 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper third. Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels and season all over with 1 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper.

Toss the carrots on a rimmed half-sheet pan with the oil and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon of salt and spread them out. Set the chicken on top of the carrots, skin side up, leaving a little space between pieces.
Roast for 25 minutes, until the skin is golden and starting to crisp. Meanwhile, stir together the mustard, honey and garlic in a small bowl.

Brush or spoon the glaze over the chicken skin and let any extra drip onto the carrots. Roast for 10 to 15 minutes more, until the glaze is bubbling and browned in spots and the thickest thigh reads at least 165°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Toss the carrots in the pan juices and serve them with the thighs.

title: Aloo Gobi: Cauliflower and Potatoes with Cumin and Turmeric
description: A dry North Indian-style skillet of potatoes and cauliflower, browned in oil with cumin seeds, onion and turmeric, then steamed tender under a lid. A whole head of cauliflower feeds four for a few dollars.
notes: Cut the potatoes a little smaller than the cauliflower so they finish at the same time. Resist stirring often; letting the vegetables sit against the pan is what browns them. Use only a splash of water when covering, since too much makes the cauliflower soggy. If you have them, a finished sprinkle of garam masala, chopped fresh cilantro or a squeeze of lemon all suit this dish and do not change the allergens. Serve with rice, flatbread or dal for a full meal. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat in a covered skillet or microwave until hot throughout (165°F).

ingredients.name: medium head cauliflower (about 2 lb), cut into 1 1/2-inch florets
russet or yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes (450 g)

instructions: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds, until they darken a shade and smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
Add the potatoes, turmeric and salt and stir to coat everything in the yellow oil. Spread the potatoes out and cook for 5 minutes, stirring once, until they start to brown.
Add the cauliflower and toss well. Cook uncovered for 5 minutes without much stirring, so the florets pick up some brown spots.

Sprinkle in the water, cover the skillet and turn the heat to medium-low. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring gently once or twice, until a knife slides easily into the potatoes and the cauliflower is tender but not falling apart.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium and cook for 2 to 3 minutes to drive off any moisture. Taste for salt and serve hot.

title: Greek-Style Fasolakia: Green Beans and Potatoes Braised in Tomato
description: Green beans and potatoes slowly simmered in olive oil, onion, garlic and tomatoes until silky. A Greek ladera dish that tastes even better the next day and costs about $2 a bowl.
equipment: large Dutch oven or heavy pot with a lid
notes: These beans are meant to be soft, not crisp; they are done when they bend easily and taste sweet. The generous olive oil is part of the dish, so do not cut it by much. Frozen cut green beans work well, added straight from the freezer with 5 minutes less cooking. Serve with bread for dipping, which adds wheat, or crumble block feta over the top, which adds milk. Fasolakia is good warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 5 days; reheat gently on the stove until hot (165°F). It freezes for up to 3 months, though the potatoes soften further.

ingredients.name: green beans, trimmed and cut in half (680 g)
russet or yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks (450 g)

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the green beans and potatoes and stir to coat them in the oil. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the beans turn a brighter green.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, water, remaining salt and pepper. The liquid should come most of the way up the vegetables; add a splash more water if needed.
Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat and simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the beans are very tender and the potatoes break apart easily with a spoon.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes more if the sauce looks thin; it should coat the vegetables, not pool like soup. Taste for salt and let it rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Pantry Peanut Noodles with Scallions
description: Noodles tossed in a quick sauce of peanut butter, soy sauce and rice vinegar loosened with hot water, then showered with scallions. Good hot or cold, packs well, about $1.25 a serving.
notes: Natural peanut butter (just peanuts and salt) makes a cleaner, less sweet sauce; if yours is sweetened, use a little less soy sauce. The sauce thickens as it cools, so loosen cold leftovers with a spoonful of warm water before eating. Sunflower seed butter can replace the peanut butter for a peanut-free version, and gluten-free tamari with rice noodles makes it wheat-free (soy remains). Sliced cucumber, shredded cabbage or leftover cooked chicken make good additions; chicken makes it no longer vegan. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days. Eat cold or reheat in the microwave until steaming (165°F).

ingredients.name: hot water, plus more as needed
kosher salt, for the pasta water

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the kosher salt. Cook the noodles according to the package until just tender.

While the noodles cook, whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce and rice vinegar in a large mixing bowl. Whisk in the hot water a little at a time until the sauce is smooth and about as thick as heavy cream.
Drain the noodles in a colander. For hot noodles, add them straight to the bowl; for cold noodles, rinse them under cold water and shake them dry first.
Add about two thirds of the scallions and toss with tongs until every strand is coated. If the sauce looks tight, add warm water a tablespoon at a time.
Taste and add a little more soy sauce or vinegar if you want it saltier or brighter. Serve topped with the remaining scallions, or pack into containers for lunches.

title: Five-Ingredient Black Bean Soup with Cumin and Salsa
description: Canned black beans simmered with onion, garlic and cumin, then thickened by mashing part of the pot. Jarred salsa brings the tomato, chile and acid. Ready in 30 minutes for about $1.50 a bowl.
notes: Do not drain the beans: the liquid in the can helps thicken the soup, so just pour them in. Mash or blend about half the pot for a creamy body with whole beans left for texture. Use a mild or hot salsa to set the heat. A spoon of full-fat sour cream, grated cheddar or crushed tortilla chips on top is good; dairy adds milk, and flour tortilla chips may add wheat. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 5 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Thin with a splash of water when reheating, and bring to a simmer (165°F).

ingredients.name: black beans (15 oz each), with their liquid
tomato salsa or pico de gallo, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Pour in the black beans with their liquid, the salsa and the water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Mash about half of the beans in the pot with a potato masher, or pulse briefly with an immersion blender, until the soup is thick and creamy with plenty of whole beans left.
Simmer 2 to 3 minutes more, adding water if it is thicker than you like. Season with the remaining salt and pepper to taste, and serve with a spoonful of salsa on top.

title: Simple Shakshuka: Eggs Poached in Cumin Tomato Sauce
description: Eggs gently cooked in a skillet of onion, garlic, cumin and crushed tomatoes. A North African breakfast that works any time of day; six eggs and one can feed three for about $1.50 each.
notes: Cook the sauce down until thick before adding the eggs; a watery sauce lets the eggs spread and overcook. The whites should be fully set and opaque, and anyone young, pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system should cook the yolks until firm. Serve with bread for scooping, which adds wheat, or crumble block feta over the top, which adds milk. A diced red bell pepper cooked with the onion is a classic addition. The tomato sauce can be made up to 4 days ahead and refrigerated, then reheated before adding fresh eggs; cooked eggs are best eaten right away. Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 7 to 8 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and 3/4 teaspoon of the salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 10 to 12 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough that a spoon dragged through it leaves a clear path for a second or two.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Make 6 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Sprinkle the eggs with the remaining salt and some pepper.

Cover the skillet and cook for 6 to 9 minutes, until the whites are completely set and opaque and the yolks are cooked to your liking. Check from 5 minutes on, since the eggs firm quickly near the end.
Spoon into shallow bowls, with two eggs and plenty of sauce per serving, and grind more pepper over the top.

title: Banana Oat Cookies with Chocolate Chips
description: Soft, chewy cookies made from ripe bananas and rolled oats, with chocolate chips and cinnamon. No flour, eggs or added sugar, and a good use for spotty bananas at pennies a cookie.
notes: Use bananas that are heavily speckled or brown; they are sweeter and bind the oats better. These cookies do not spread, so press them to the thickness you want before baking. They are soft and cakey rather than crisp, and they firm up as they cool. Regular semisweet chocolate chips often contain milk and soy, so check the label; using them changes the allergens. Rolled oats are naturally gluten-free, but use certified gluten-free oats if you need the cookies gluten-free. Keep in a covered container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 3 months and thaw at room temperature.

ingredients.name: mashed very ripe banana (about 3 medium, 225 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a mixing bowl, mash the bananas with a fork until almost smooth, with only a few small lumps. Stir in the vanilla, cinnamon and salt.
Add the oats and stir until every flake is coated. Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes so the oats soak up some of the banana, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the baking sheet, about 1 inch apart. Press each mound with damp fingers into a round about 1/2 inch thick.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the cookies are set, golden on the bottom and lightly browned at the edges.
Cool on the baking sheet for 10 minutes, then move to a rack. They hold together better once completely cool.
